1. Core Clinical Tension: A 59-year-old male with well-controlled HIV on antiretroviral therapy (CD4 219 cells/µL, undetectable viral load) presented with a 1-year history of worsening mechanical and inflammatory back pain, night sweats, weight loss, and restricted spinal mobility. Imaging confirmed destructive spondylodiscitis at L2-L3 with bony sequestra and a massive paravertebral abscess. The principal clinical tension is distinguishing recurrent indolent spinal infection caused by an endemic granulomatous pathogen (specifically drug-resistant mycobacterial spondylitis) from opportunistic pyogenic spondylodiscitis or metastatic spinal malignancy in a person living with HIV.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Outpatient orthopedic evaluation, physical exam documenting focal L1-L3 spinal tenderness and restricted mobility, baseline inflammatory markers, CD4 count, and initial spinal imaging (X-ray, CT, MRI) demonstrating L2/L3 osteolytic destruction and paravertebral abscess, strictly prior to surgical decompression/debridement, postoperative fistula drainage, and drug susceptibility testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pyogenic spondylodiscitis (such as Staphylococcus aureus) presents with acute or subacute rapid spine destruction, high fever, and marked leukocytosis, rather than a protracted 1-year course characterized by cold abscesses and necrotic sequestra. Spinal neoplastic metastases or myeloma typically spare the intervertebral disc spaces, whereas infectious spondylodiscitis predominantly targets the disc and adjacent vertebral endplates with prominent abscess formation.
case_prompt:
A 59-year-old male presented to the orthopedics outpatient department with a 1-year history of progressive low back pain aggravated by physical activity, accompanied by intermittent low-grade fever, night sweats, and persistent fatigue. He had an underlying medical history of HIV infection diagnosed 5 years previously, maintained on a stable antiretroviral regimen of lamivudine, tenofovir, and efavirenz, with sustained undetectable viral load and CD4+ T-lymphocyte counts historically fluctuating between 200 and 300 cells/µL. He had previously received an empiric multi-agent antibiotic regimen at another facility for suspected infectious spondylitis, but continued to experience unremitting spinal symptoms.

On physical examination, the patient walked with an antalgic limp. Point tenderness and percussion tenderness were localized over the spinous processes of L1 through L3 and bilateral paravertebral regions, without radicular pain radiating into the lower extremities. Motor examination revealed 5/5 strength throughout all bilateral lower extremity muscle groups. Range of motion of the lumbar spine was severely restricted in all planes (forward flexion 10°, backward extension 20°, lateral flexion 10°–20°, rotation 10°–20°). Straight leg raise tests, femoral nerve stretch tests, and lower extremity deep tendon reflexes were normal bilaterally, with down-going plantar reflexes.

Initial laboratory studies showed C-reactive protein of 11.9 mg/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 38.0 mm/hr, serum albumin of 33.0 g/L, and a CD4+ T-cell count of 219 cells/µL. Lumbar spine plain radiography demonstrated uneven bone density and pronounced narrowing of the L2–L3 intervertebral disc space. Lumbar CT and contrast-enhanced MRI revealed osteolytic destruction and cavitations within L2–L3 with multiple irregular necrotic sequestra, associated with a large, prominent paravertebral abscess extending along the psoas musculature.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to subacute-to-chronic lumbar discitis, vertebral osteolysis, and paravertebral fluid collection in an immunocompromised HIV-infected patient; ruled out by the indolent 1-year progression, presence of multiple bony sequestra and cold paravertebral abscesses rather than acute suppurative pyogenic necrosis, and subsequent microbiological isolation of resistant mycobacteria.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A 59-year-old male patient had low back pain without obvious cause for nearly one year, which was aggravated during activities, accompanied by intermittent fever, night sweat, and fatigue.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered in an older adult with constitutional symptoms, weight loss, elevated ESR, and vertebral osteolytic destruction; ruled out by classic involvement and collapse of the L2–L3 intervertebral disc space with extensive paravertebral/psoas abscess collections, as hematogenous neoplasms characteristically spare the disc space.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Preoperative lumbar X-ray showed uneven density and narrowing of the L2/3 intervertebral space (Figure 1A and B). Lumbar CT and enhanced MRI showed cavities and osteolytic destruction in L2/3 with multiple irregular sequestrum, the paravertebral abscess was large and prominent.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Surgical debridement and subsequent abscess drainage of postoperative sinus formation confirmed persistent caseating spinal infection, with definitive drug susceptibility testing demonstrating secondary multidrug resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to isoniazid and rifampin.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: During the follow-up, it was learned that the patient was resistant to rifampin and isoniazid in the tuberculosis drug resistance test in the local hospital, and he was advised to change to oral rifapentine and prothionamide.

editor_comments: Case prompt sanitized to exclude pathogen names while accurately capturing the 1-year history of spondylodiscitis, HIV background, physical exam, and imaging before surgical exploration and resistance testing.
